# 11 — The `coroutine` library (Lua 5.5.1 reference behaviour)

Reference binary: `Lua 5.5.1  Copyright (C) 1994-2026 Lua.org, PUC-Rio`
(`_VERSION == "Lua 5.5"`). Everything below was observed by running the binary.

> **Read the "5.5 differences" box first** — several behaviours differ from the
> familiar Lua 5.4 semantics, most notably `coroutine.close` on the *running*
> coroutine, the `"cannot close main thread"` message, `<no error object>`, and
> yieldable `__close` handlers.

---

## 1. Library contents

`coroutine` contains exactly 8 fields, all functions:

```
close	function
create	function
isyieldable	function
resume	function
running	function
status	function
wrap	function
yield	function
```

There is no `coroutine.kill`, no `coroutine.reset`, no metatable on `coroutine`.

### 1.1 Signature / argument-checking table

| function | arity | arg #1 | absent arg #1 | explicit `nil` arg #1 | extra args |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `coroutine.create(f)` | 1 | must be a function (Lua **or** C function) | error | error | ignored |
| `coroutine.resume(co, ...)` | 1+ | must be a thread | error | error | passed to coroutine |
| `coroutine.yield(...)` | 0+ | – | – | – | all passed to resumer |
| `coroutine.status(co)` | 1 | must be a thread (**required**) | error | error | ignored |
| `coroutine.wrap(f)` | 1 | must be a function | error | error | ignored |
| `coroutine.isyieldable([co])` | 0–1 | thread, **optional** → running thread | defaults | error | ignored |
| `coroutine.running()` | 0 | – | – | – | ignored |
| `coroutine.close([co])` | 0–1 | thread, **optional** → running thread | defaults | error | ignored |

Note the asymmetry: `status` requires its argument, while `isyieldable` and
`close` treat *no value* as "the running thread" but reject an explicit `nil`.

Argument error template (standard `luaL_argerror`):

```
bad argument #1 to 'coroutine.close' (thread expected, got number)
bad argument #1 to 'coroutine.create' (function expected, got no value)
bad argument #1 to 'coroutine.isyieldable' (thread expected, got boolean)
```

* When the failing call has **no Lua caller frame** (e.g. called straight from
  `pcall`), the name printed is the fully-qualified `coroutine.<name>` (found by
  scanning `package.loaded`) and **no `file:line:` prefix** is added.
* When the failing call *does* have a Lua caller frame, the short debug name is
  used and a position prefix **is** added:

```lua
local function f() return coroutine.status(1) end
print(pcall(f))
--> false	018_args.lua:21: bad argument #1 to 'status' (thread expected, got number)
```

Taking a local alias does **not** change this (`local cl = coroutine.close;
pcall(cl, 5)` still reports `'coroutine.close'`), because the name comes from the
global-name scan, not from the local variable.

---

## 2. Threads as values

| expression | result |
|---|---|
| `type(co)` | `"thread"` |
| `tostring(co)` | `"thread: 0x55f84b284828"` — prefix `thread: ` then `%p` |
| `string.format("%s", co)` | same as `tostring` |
| `math.type(co)` | `nil` |
| `tonumber(co)` | `nil` (no error) |
=== TESTS ===
001_basic_lifecycle.lua
=== EXAMPLE TEST ===
-- coroutine: create / resume / yield / status / value passing
local co = coroutine.create(function(a, b)
  print("body", a, b, select('#', a, b))
  local c, d = coroutine.yield(a + b)
  print("resumed with", c, d)
  return "ret1", "ret2"
end)

print("type", type(co))
print("tostring prefix", tostring(co):sub(1, 8))
print("tostring shape", tostring(co):match("^thread: 0x%x+$") ~= nil)
print("self equal", co == co)

print("status", coroutine.status(co))
print("resume1", coroutine.resume(co, 1, 2))
print("status", coroutine.status(co))
print("resume2", coroutine.resume(co, 10, 20))
print("status", coroutine.status(co))
print("resume3", coroutine.resume(co))
print("status", coroutine.status(co))

print("n two nils", nres(coroutine.resume(coroutine.create(function() return nil, nil end))))
